lead.t: Transcription ends when RNA polymerase II reaches a termination signal — this is a special sequence in the RNA: AAUAAA (called the polyadenylation signal).

snip.t: Transcription ends when RNA polymerase II reaches a termination signal — this is a special sequence in the RNA: AAUAAA (called the polyadenylation signal).
Includes a polyadenylation signal (AAUAAA) that leads to mRNA cleavage and polyadenylation.

qs.q: During an experiment analyzing transcription termination in eukaryotes, a researcher targets the enzyme responsible for cleaving the nascent pre-mRNA downstream of the polyadenylation signal. Which enzymatic activity is being disrupted?
o: The 5-prime to 3-prime exonuclease activity of RNA polymerase II
The intrinsic proofreading 3-prime to 5-prime exonuclease of transcriptase
The endonuclease activity associated with polyadenylation specificity factor
The ligase activity sealing remaining RNA fragments into a mature transcript
The methyltransferase activity capping the newly exposed transcript terminus
qs.e: Pre-mRNA cleavage at the polyadenylation site is mediated by multiprotein complexes possessing specific endonuclease activities.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Molecular Biology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: What is the function of the polyadenylation signal (AAUAAA) located in the downstream terminator region of a eukaryotic gene?
o: Leading to mRNA cleavage and polyadenylation
Binding the sigma factor to initiate transcription
Melting the DNA template strand at the start site
qs.e: The polyadenylation signal includes AAUAAA, which signals RNA polymerase to stop transcription and leads to mRNA cleavage and polyadenylation. It does not participate in transcription initiation or sigma factor recruitment.
